definition_zh: 牛仔裤；粗斜纹棉布裤
definition_en: trousers made of strong cotton cloth, usually blue, worn informally by people of any age
core_image: 两条磨得发白的厚棉布裤腿，口袋上钉着黄铜铆钉
scene: 衣柜最下面压着一条穿旧的裤子，膝盖处已经泛白。 He pulled on his old jeans and went out to the corner store.
sceneCN: 这里 jeans 是「牛仔裤」（第 1 个义项：粗斜纹棉布做的裤子），句意为他套上旧牛仔裤就去街角小店了。画面里的物件：衣柜、泛白的膝部、门口。

pos.zh: 名词：牛仔裤；粗斜纹布裤（只用复数）

derivatives.zh: 由 jeans 去掉词尾 -s 而来，指牛仔布或牛仔裤单条
同类词，指牛仔布本身，法国布料名 Nîmes 缩合而成
由 jeans 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着牛仔裤的」，多用于书面描写

senses.title: Trousers of strong cotton cloth
senses.definition: trousers made of a heavy twilled cotton fabric, usually dyed blue
senses.definitionCN: 用厚重的斜纹棉布做成的裤子，通常染成蓝色
senses.example: She bought a pair of jeans with a straight leg.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一条直筒牛仔裤。
senses.why: The word names the cloth before it names the trousers, and the trousers kept the plural shape of the cloth word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指布料再指裤子，而裤子沿用了布料词的复数外形。

senses.title: A blue-cotton everyday uniform
senses.definition: such trousers worn as tough working clothes rather than as fashion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为耐磨工作服而非时装穿用的这种裤子
senses.example: Miners once wore jeans because the cloth refused to tear.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工当年穿牛仔裤，是因为这种布不容易撕破。
senses.why: The plural word carried the work-clothes sense long before fashion adopted it.
senses.whyCN: 在时装接手之前，这个复数词很久以来一直指工装。

senses.title: A fashion item with a cut or wash
senses.definition: a pair of such trousers treated as a styled garment, described by cut, wash, or finish
senses.definitionCN: 按剪裁、水洗或做旧处理来描述的时装裤装
senses.example: His ripped jeans cost more than my winter coat.
senses.exampleCN: 他那条破洞牛仔裤比我冬天的大衣还贵。
senses.why: Once the garment became a style object, the word picked up the whole vocabulary of cuts and washes.
senses.whyCN: 这条裤子成了时尚对象之后，这个词就带上了整套剪裁与水洗的说法。

senses.title: Denim cloth itself
senses.definition: the twilled cotton fabric from which such trousers are made
senses.definitionCN: 用来做这种裤子的斜纹棉布
senses.example: The jacket is made of dark jeans cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 这件夹克是用深色牛仔布做的。
senses.why: The fabric sense is the older layer of meaning and still survives in compounds.
senses.whyCN: 布料义是这个词更早的一层意思，至今还活在一些复合词里。

senses.title: A casual dress code
senses.definition: an informal standard of dress in which such trousers are acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 允许穿这类裤子的非正式着装标准
senses.example: The office allows jeans on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 公司允许周五穿牛仔裤上班。
senses.why: From a garment, the word grew into a label for a whole dress code.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从一件衣服长成了整套着装标准的标签。

intro.en: Jeans is a plural garment word that came into English from the name of a cloth, and the cloth name came from a city.
intro.cn: jeans 是一个复数形式的衣物词，先经由布料名进入英语，而布料名又来自一座城市的名字。

items.en: The cloth name Gene was used in French for a twilled cotton fabric made at Genoa.
items.cn: 法语用 Gene 指热那亚出产的斜纹棉布。

items.en: English borrowed the cloth word as jean or jene in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪把布料词借作 jean 或 jene。

items.en: The plural jeans first named such cloth and later the trousers cut from it.
items.cn: 复数形式 jeans 先指这种布，后来指用它裁成的裤子。

items.en: American workwear of the nineteenth century fixed the blue trousers sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪的美国工装固定了「蓝色长裤」这一义项。

items.en: Denim entered English by another route, from serge de Nîmes.
items.cn: denim 经由另一条路径进入英语，来自「尼姆的哔叽」这一布料名。

note.en: The look-alike group holds cloth and garment words that travel with jeans; the near-meaning group holds other everyday trousers.
note.cn: 形近组收与 jeans 同行的布料和衣物词；近义组收其他日常裤装词。

entries.definition: Heavy twilled cotton used for jeans.
entries.definitionCN: 指做牛仔裤的厚斜纹棉布，与 jeans 常成对出现，但拼写与来源都不同。

entries.definition: The singular form, naming the cloth or one pair.
entries.definitionCN: jeans 的单数形式，指牛仔布或一条裤子。

entries.definition: A general British word for a two-legged garment.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指裤子的英式说法，语法上同样常用复数。

entries.definition: The usual American word for trousers.
entries.definitionCN: 美式英语里最常见的「裤子」。

entries.definition: Smart casual trousers, not denim.
entries.definitionCN: 指较正式的休闲长裤，一般不用牛仔布。

entries.definition: Light cotton trousers in plain colours.
entries.definitionCN: 指素色薄棉布休闲裤。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the city of Genoa to the Friday dress code.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从热那亚这座城走到周五的休闲着装。

normal.en: The cloth name came from Genoa, Italian Genova.
normal.cn: 布料名来自热那亚，意大利语作 Genova。

normal.en: Jeans is normally plural, like trousers and glasses.
normal.cn: jeans 通常用复数，和 trousers、glasses 一样。

normal.en: A pair of jeans is the standard counting pattern.
normal.cn: 计数的标准说法是 a pair of jeans。

normal.en: Denim and jeans are near twins but took different routes.
normal.cn: denim 与 jeans 像双胞胎，但来路不同。

normal.en: Blue jeans fixed the colour sense in American workwear.
normal.cn: 蓝色牛仔裤在美国工装里固定了这个颜色义。

abstract.en: A pair of jeans is a city folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 一条牛仔裤就是一座城市折进了口袋。

abstract.en: The rivets are little guarantees that the cloth will hold.
abstract.cn: 铆钉是布料不裂开的小小保证。

abstract.en: Faded knees are a calendar written in cloth.
abstract.cn: 磨白的膝盖是写在布上的日历。

examples.en: These jeans are too tight around the waist.
examples.cn: 这条牛仔裤腰部太紧了。

examples.en: He wears jeans to work on casual days.
examples.cn: 轻松的上班日他穿牛仔裤。

examples.en: The shop sells jeans in every shade of blue.
examples.cn: 这家店卖各种深浅的蓝色牛仔裤。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「紧死」—— 牛仔裤穿太紧，就真的紧死了

root: 来自法语布料名 Gene，源于意大利城市 Genoa（热那亚）；十六世纪进入英语作 jean，复数 jeans 后指用它缝制的长裤。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the cotton trousers, their use as work clothes, their life as fashion, the cloth itself, and the dress code they stand for.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：棉布长裤本身、作为工装、作为时装、布料本身，以及它所代表的休闲着装。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick blue cotton cut into two legs and held by rivets.
core.cn: 核心意象：厚蓝棉布裁成两条裤腿，用铆钉钉牢。

branches.en: THE CLOTH LINE: a fabric that became a pair of trousers.
branches.cn: 布料这条线：一种布变成了裤子。

branches.en: THE MINE LINE: work clothes that refuse to tear.
branches.cn: 矿井这条线：撕不破的工装。

branches.en: THE SHOP WINDOW: cuts, washes, and rips sold as style.
branches.cn: 橱窗这条线：剪裁、水洗、破洞都能卖。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: a garment that marks a whole relaxed day.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：一件衣服标出整个轻松的日子。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY LINE: tough cloth that also looks personal.
branches.cn: 日常这条线：耐磨的布也能显得有个性。

intro.en: Jeans is borrowed whole, so English adds only endings; the visible endings are the plural -s and the adjective -ed.
intro.cn: jeans 是整体借来的词，英语只添词尾；看得见的是复数 -s 与形容词 -ed。

latinIntro.en: The word comes from a place name rather than a Latin root, so the Latin relatives below are city-name forms only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自地名而非拉丁词根，下面的拉丁条目只是城市名的形式。

items.example: The weaver sold jean by the metre.
The cloth was shipped from Genoa.
It feels like a denimy blue.

items.exampleCN: 蓝色牛仔裤是最常见的。

definition_zh: 参加；出席；上（学）；照料
definition_en: to be present at an event, or to go to a school, or to take care of someone
core_image: 礼堂里坐满来开会的家长
scene: 礼堂里坐满了家长，一位母亲来参加学校的会议。 She attended the school meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 attended 是「参加」（第 1 个义项：到场出席）；句意为她参加了学校的会议。

pos.zh: 动词：参加；出席；上（学）；照料

derivatives.zh: 出席；出勤
服务员
注意

senses.title: To be present at an event
senses.definition: to be present at a meeting, a class or an event
senses.definitionCN: 到场参加某个会议、课程或活动
senses.example: She attended the school meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她参加了学校的会议。
senses.why: Stretching toward a place puts a person inside it, so being present is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 向某处伸展就把人放进那个地方，所以到场就是第一义。

senses.title: To go to a school
senses.definition: to go regularly to a school or a course
senses.definitionCN: 定期去某所学校或某门课程
senses.example: He attends a school near his home.
senses.exampleCN: 他在家附近的一所学校上学。
senses.why: Stretching toward a school again and again becomes the regular act of attending it.
senses.whyCN: 一次次向学校伸展，就成了定期上学的行为。

senses.title: To take care of
senses.definition: to give care and help to a person or a matter
senses.definitionCN: 对人给予照料，或处理某件事
senses.example: A nurse attended to the injured boy.
senses.exampleCN: 一名护士照料那个受伤的男孩。
senses.why: Turning toward a person in need is the same stretch of attention, now in the sense of care.
senses.whyCN: 朝向有需要的人同样是注意力的伸展，此时就是照料之意。

intro.en: The recorded history of attend is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 attend 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Attendere meant to stretch toward or to give heed.
items.cn: attendere 意为向某处伸展或留心。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or to extend.
items.cn: tendere 意为伸展或延展。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into daily use.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带入日常使用。

items.en: English used attend for being present and for care.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 attend 既指到场，也指照料。

items.en: Today it also covers going to school regularly.
items.cn: 今天它也涵盖定期上学。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The third person form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数形式。

entries.definition: The noun for being present.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指出席。

entries.definition: The noun for a person who serves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指服务人员。

entries.definition: It stresses becoming part of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 强调成为群体的一员。

entries.definition: It stresses being there at the time.
entries.definitionCN: 强调当时在场。

entries.definition: It stresses giving help to others.
entries.definitionCN: 强调为他人提供帮助。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ad- means toward and tendere means to stretch: to attend is to stretch toward a place or a duty.
normal.cn: ad- 表示朝向，tendere 表示伸展：attend 就是把身心伸向某个场合或责任。

normal.en: The same family also gives attendance and attendant.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 attendance 与 attendant。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase attend a meeting.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「参加会议」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of attend in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 attend 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to be present at an event, or to go to a school, or to take care of someone.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「参加」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a hall filled with parents who came to a school meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象礼堂里坐满来开会的家长。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She attended the school meeting.
examples.cn: 她参加了学校的会议。

examples.en: He attends a school near his home.
examples.cn: 他在家附近的一所学校上学。

examples.en: A nurse attended to the injured boy.
examples.cn: 一名护士照料那个受伤的男孩。

root: attend 来自拉丁语 attendere「向某处伸展、留心」，与 tendere「伸展」相关，经古法语进入英语；十四世纪既指到场也指照料，今天还涵盖定期上学。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of attend grows from one core image: a hall filled with parents who came to a school meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: attend 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：礼堂里坐满来开会的家长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hall filled with parents who came to a school meeting
core.cn: 核心意象：礼堂里坐满来开会的家长

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: To be present at an event.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：参加、出席。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: To go to a school.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：上（学）。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: To be present at an event / To go to a school.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：参加、出席、上（学）。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: To take care of.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：照料。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the outer edge of the meaning: To be present at an event / To take care of.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖意义的边缘：参加、出席、照料。

intro.en: attend can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: attend 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It comes from tendere, to stretch.
It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 公司；陪伴；同伴；宾客
definition_en: a business organisation, or the state of being with other people
core_image: 和你待在一起的人，或大家一起做事的机构
scene: 周五晚上，他不愿一个人待着，去找了同学。 A big company will build a new school near our town.
sceneCN: 这里 company 是「公司」（第 1 个义项：企业组织）；句意是一家大公司要在镇附近建新学校。

derivatives.zh: 来自同一拉丁词根，义为「同伴；伙伴」
由 ac- 加 company 词根构成，义为「陪伴；伴随」
由 companion 加 -ship 构成，义为「友谊；陪伴之情」

senses.title: A business organisation
senses.definition: an organisation that makes or sells things, or offers services
senses.definitionCN: 制造、销售商品或提供服务的组织
senses.example: This company makes school bags for students.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司为学生生产书包。
senses.why: Bread eaten together started the word: a business is a group that works side by side.
senses.whyCN: 本义是「同吃一份面包的人」：公司就是并肩做事的群体。

senses.title: Being with someone so you are not alone
senses.definition: the state of being with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与他人相处、不孤单的状态
senses.example: Your company makes the long trip pleasant.
senses.exampleCN: 有你的陪伴，长途旅行也变得愉快。
senses.why: Having someone with you is the heart of the old meaning.
senses.whyCN: 「有人与你同在」正是这个词古老本义的核心。

senses.title: Guests or visitors
senses.definition: people who are visiting your home
senses.definitionCN: 到你家来做客的人
senses.example: We have company tonight, so tidy your room.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚有客人来，把房间收拾好。
senses.why: Guests are people who share your table, so the eating-together idea returned.
senses.whyCN: 客人就是与你同桌的人，「同食」之义在这里回归。

senses.title: A group such as soldiers or actors
senses.definition: a group of soldiers or performers working together
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的士兵或演员团体
senses.example: The drama company will stage our play.
senses.exampleCN: 剧团将上演我们的话剧。
senses.why: Any group standing together keeps the old togetherness.
senses.whyCN: 凡并肩而立的群体都保留了「在一起」的古义。

intro.en: Company began with bread: people who eat together.
intro.cn: company 起于「面包」：同吃一锅饭的人。

items.en: Latin panis meant bread, the base of the story.
items.cn: 拉丁语 panis 意为面包，是这个词故事的起点。

items.en: Late Latin companio meant one who shares bread with you, a mate.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 companio 指与你分享面包的人，即同伴。

items.en: Old French compaignie meant a group of companions or fellowship.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignie 指一群同伴或伙伴关系。

items.en: Middle English companye meant fellowship, guests and groups of workers.
items.cn: 中古英语 companye 涵盖伙伴、宾客与工人团体。

items.en: Modern English company fixed the business sense as firms grew.
items.cn: 现代英语随着公司兴起把商业义项固定下来。

note.en: The first group collects the same-root family; the second collects words close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词，第二组收近义词。

entries.definition: A person who goes with you.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同伴」，与 company 同源于 companio。

entries.definition: To go together with someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「陪伴」，同根词。

entries.definition: A separate section of a space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「隔间」，形近但词根不同。

entries.definition: The pleasant feeling of having a companion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陪伴之情」，同根派生词。

entries.definition: A business company.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商行；公司」，较正式。

entries.definition: Trade or a commercial organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「生意；企业」。

entries.definition: Friendly company with others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交情；友谊」。

normalIntro.en: Remember company through shared bread and shared work.
normalIntro.cn: 从「同食面包」与「并肩工作」记 company。

normal.en: com- means together and panis means bread.
normal.cn: com- 表示一起，panis 表示面包。

normal.en: companion and company share a root.
normal.cn: companion 与 company 同词根。

normal.en: keep someone company means stay with them.
normal.cn: keep someone company 指陪伴某人。

normal.en: A company is also called a firm.
normal.cn: 公司也可以叫 firm。

normal.en: The plural of company is companies.
normal.cn: company 的复数是 companies。

abstract.en: Picture friends breaking one loaf of bread.
abstract.cn: 想象朋友们分食一块面包。

abstract.en: See workers walking into one big gate.
abstract.cn: 想象工人们走进同一扇大门。

abstract.en: Feel a warm shoulder beside you on a long walk.
abstract.cn: 感觉长途跋涉中有肩膀在旁。

definition_en: to shout with joy or support; to make someone happier; a shout of joy; a feeling of happiness
core_image: 看台上齐声呐喊为队伍加油，把低落的士气重新点亮

senses.title: To shout with joy or support
senses.definition: to shout loudly to show joy or to encourage a person or team
senses.definitionCN: 大声呼喊以表达喜悦或为人和队伍鼓劲
senses.example: The whole class began to cheer for the last runner.
senses.exampleCN: 全班开始为最后一棒呐喊助威。
senses.why: The word first named the expression on the face; when a crowd's joy bursts out, the face's word becomes the shout.
senses.whyCN: 词最初指脸上的神情；当人群的喜悦迸发而出，表情之名便化作呐喊之声。

senses.title: To make someone happier
senses.definition: to make a sad or tired person feel better
senses.definitionCN: 让难过或疲惫的人好受起来

senses.exampleCN: 一顿热饭让疲惫的队员精神一振。
senses.why: Bringing joy to one face is the inward side of the outward shout: same feeling, quieter form.
senses.whyCN: 把喜悦带到一张脸上，正是欢呼声的内敛一面：同一种情感，更安静的形式。

senses.title: A shout of encouragement or joy
senses.definition: a loud shout of joy or support from a group

senses.example: A great cheer went up when the goal was scored.
senses.exampleCN: 进球时爆发出一片欢呼。
senses.why: The act of shouting is named, then the sound itself keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 呼喊的动作先被命名，喊出的声音随后沿用其名。

senses.title: A mood of happiness
senses.definition: a feeling of happiness and hope
senses.definitionCN: 快乐与希望的心情
senses.example: Her kind words filled the room with cheer.
senses.exampleCN: 她温暖的话语让满屋生辉。
senses.why: Behind both shout and smile sits the feeling itself, and the word can name that feeling alone.
senses.whyCN: 呼喊与笑容背后是情感本身，这个词也能单独指称这份心情。

intro.en: Cheer once meant the face or expression, then the inner mood, then the loud joy that shows both.

definition_zh: 办公室；办公场所；办事处；部门；职务；职位；公务；职责
definition_en: a room or building where people do their desk work; also a position of authority, a branch of an organization or government, and the duty attached to a post
core_image: 一张靠窗的写字台，抽屉里放着印章，桌牌上写明了这张桌子承担的职责
scene: 清晨楼道里还没开灯，靠窗那张写字台已经摊开文件，印章和文件夹摆得整整齐齐。 The office stayed quiet until the first cup of tea was finished.
sceneCN: 这里是「办公室、办公场所」（第 1 个义项：人们做案头工作的房间）；句意为这间屋一直安静到第一杯茶喝完。可辨物件：靠窗写字台、印章、文件夹、未开灯的走廊。

pos.zh: 办公室；办公场所；办事处；部门；职务；职责

derivatives.zh: 由 office 加 -ial 构成，义为「官方的」或「官员」
出自拉丁 officium（职责），义为「爱管闲事的；好用权威的」
由 office 与 holder 复合而成，义为「担任公职者」

senses.title: A room or building where desk work is done
senses.definition: a room or set of rooms in which people sit at desks and carry out the work of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 人们坐在桌前处理某个机构事务的房间或一组房间
senses.example: She left a note on the office door before the others arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 在别人来之前，她在办公室门上留了一张纸条。
senses.why: Officium in Latin meant the duty itself, and the room was named after the task done inside it, so the place inherits the name of the service rather than the furniture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 officium 指的是职责本身，这间屋子因为里面办的差事而得名，所以它继承的是「公务」的名字，而不是桌椅的名字。

senses.title: A position of authority, especially in government
senses.definition: a post or rank that gives a person formal power within a government or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在政府或机构中给予某人正式权力的岗位或位次
senses.example: The new mayor takes office at the start of next month.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长下个月初就职。
senses.why: Once officium names a duty, people begin to speak of holding that duty as a thing they possess, and the word slides from the task to the post that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 既然 officium 能指一份职责，人们就把它当成可以捧在手里的东西，说「担任」这份职责，词义便从差事滑到承载差事的位子上。

senses.title: A branch or department of a government or organization
senses.definition: a local branch or department through which a larger body performs one of its duties
senses.definitionCN: 较大的机构为履行某一项职责而设的地方分支或部门
senses.example: The passport office opens at eight in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 护照办事处早上八点开门。
senses.why: An institution that owes the public a service must put a counter somewhere, so the name of the duty spreads to the counters, and post office or tax office follows the same path.
senses.whyCN: 一个对公众负有职责的机构总得在某处摆上柜台，于是「职责」的名字扩散到这些柜台，邮局、税务局走的都是这条路径。

senses.title: The duty or service owed to others
senses.titleCN: 公务；职责；人情上的帮忙
senses.definition: the service or help that one person owes or gives to another, still kept in phrases such as good offices
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对他人应尽或给予的服务与帮助，仍保留在 good offices 一类说法中
senses.example: Through the good offices of a neighbour, the two families finally met.
senses.exampleCN: 经一位邻居从中帮忙，两家人终于见了面。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the word: a duty is something performed for someone else, and the modern phrase good offices still offers help without any desk or building in sight.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的一层：职责就是替别人做事，而今天 good offices 仍指不带桌椅、也不带建筑的一份帮忙。

intro.en: Office grows out of a Latin compound that says doing work for someone else, which is why one word can name a duty, the post that carries it and the room where it is performed.
intro.cn: office 长在一个表示「替别人做事」的拉丁复合词上，所以同一个词既能指职责，也能指承担职责的职位和办事的房间。

items.en: Opus meant work, especially the work of making or building, and it supplies the first element of the word.
items.cn: opus 意为工作，尤指制作、建造的活儿，是这个词的第一个成分。

items.en: Facere meant to do or to make, and English still uses it in words such as factory and manufacture.
items.cn: facere 意为做、制作，英语的 factory、manufacture 里还留着它的影子。

items.en: Officium joined the two into the sense of performing work for another person, hence a service, a duty, and a post held in the Roman state.
items.cn: officium 把两者合成「为别人做事」，由此指服务、职责，也指在罗马城邦里担任的职位。

items.en: Old French office passed the noun to English with the duty sense, a religious service, and later the place where business is handled.
items.cn: 古法语 office 把这个名词传给英语，带着职责义、宗教礼拜义，后来又指办事的场所。

items.en: Modern English keeps duty, post and workplace together, so a person can hold office in an office without any contradiction.
items.cn: 现代英语把职责、职位与工作场所收在同一个词里，所以一个人可以在办公室里担任职务，二者毫不矛盾。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on the Latin noun for duty; the near-meaning group collects words for a workplace and for a job.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「职责」之上的同族词；近义组收表示工作场所与工作岗位的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin phrase compressed into one noun: work plus doing, and the result is a duty that later borrows rooms and ranks from the people who perform it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被压缩成一个名词的拉丁短语：工作加做，得到的是一份职责，而职责后来又向办事的人借来了房间与位次。

normal.en: Opus is work and facere is to do, so officium began as the doing of work for someone else.
normal.cn: opus 是工作，facere 是做，所以 officium 一开始就是替别人做事。

normal.en: The earliest sense is service owed to another, which is why office can still mean a favour in good offices.
normal.cn: 最早的义项是对他人应尽的服务，所以 office 至今还能在 good offices 里表示一份人情。

normal.en: A rank is called an office because taking it means accepting the duty that comes with it.
normal.cn: 职位之所以叫 office，是因为接受这个位子就等于接下随它而来的职责。

normal.en: A post office or a tax office keeps the duty sense in a building: the counter exists because a service is performed there.
normal.cn: 邮局、税务局把职责义放进了建筑里：柜台存在，是因为那里在办一项服务。

normal.en: The same word covers a room and a rank, so English lets a minister hold office in an office.
normal.cn: 同一个词兼指房间与位次，所以英语里部长可以在办公室里担任职务。

abstract.en: A room, a rank and a favour answer to one word because each is a place where work is owed to someone.
abstract.cn: 房间、位次和人情共用一个词，因为它们都是「欠着别人一份工作」的位置。

abstract.en: Entering an office means entering a duty; the door is only the visible edge of it.
abstract.cn: 走进一间办公室就是走进一份职责，那扇门只是它露在外面的边。

abstract.en: Power in this word never stands alone: the duty comes first, and the authority is borrowed from it.
abstract.cn: 这个词里的权力从不单独存在：职责在先，权威是从职责那里借来的。

definition_zh: 在外；向外；出去；熄灭；过时；从…出来
definition_en: away from the inside of a place, or moving from within to beyond a boundary; also no longer burning or fashionable; as a preposition, through and away from
core_image: 厨房的灯忽然灭了，一个人摸黑推开门，从屋里走到院子里
scene: 夜里厨房的灯忽然灭了，一个人摸黑推开门，从屋里走到院子里站定。 The kitchen light went out while we were still washing the dishes.
sceneCN: 这里 out 是「熄灭」（第 3 个义项：火、灯或电器不再亮、不再工作）；句意为碗还没洗完，厨房的灯就灭了，画面是黑下来的厨房与走向院子的人。

pos.zh: 在外；向外；出去；熄灭；过时

derivatives.zh: 由 out 加比较级词尾 -er 构成，义为「外部的；外面的」
由 out 加 -ing 构成，义为「外出；短途游玩」
由 out 与 set 复合而成，义为「开始；开端」
由 outward 加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向外地」

senses.title: Away from inside a place
senses.definition: not inside a building, room or container, but beyond its boundary
senses.definitionCN: 不在建筑物、房间或容器之内，而处在它的边界之外
senses.example: She is out at the moment, so please call again later.
senses.exampleCN: 她这会儿出去了，请稍后再打。
senses.why: Old English ut simply named the far side of a boundary, so the word's first task is to say that something is not inside.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ut 只指边界之外的那一侧，所以这个词最初的任务就是说明某物不在里面；第一义是纯粹的空间否定，没有别的引申。

senses.title: Moving from within to outside
senses.definition: used with verbs of movement to show a passage from inside to beyond
senses.definitionCN: 与表示移动的动词连用，表示从里面穿到外面
senses.example: He walked out without saying a word.
senses.exampleCN: 他一句话没说就走了出去。
senses.why: If the word can name the far side, it can also name the step that reaches it, so verbs of motion take out as a direction.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指界外那一侧，也就能指跨到那一侧的那一步，所以表示移动的动词带上 out 就成了方向；静态位置由此转成动态离开。

senses.title: No longer burning or working
senses.definition: of a fire, lamp or device, no longer burning, shining or running
senses.definitionCN: 指火、灯或电器不再燃烧、不再发亮、不再运转
senses.example: The fire went out before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 火在午夜前就熄了。
senses.why: A flame that is out has left the state of burning, so the word for being beyond a boundary is applied to a condition that has ended.
senses.whyCN: 熄掉的火已经离开了燃烧的状态，于是这个表示「在界外」的词被用到一种已经结束的状态上；熄灭义就是把它从空间之外搬到状态之外。

senses.title: No longer fashionable
senses.definition: of a style or idea, no longer in fashion or no longer accepted
senses.definitionCN: 指样式或观念不再流行，或不再被接受
senses.example: Long skirts are out this season.
senses.exampleCN: 长裙这一季已经过时了。
senses.why: A style that falls outside the set of things people currently accept is literally out of that set, so the spatial word becomes a judgement of taste.
senses.whyCN: 一种样式落在人们当下接受的那一套之外，就字面地「不在这一套里」，于是空间词变成了品味判断；过时义靠的正是「圈外」这个画面。

senses.title: Through and away from
senses.definition: used before a noun, as in out the door or out of the room, to mark the way from inside to outside
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词之前，如 out the door 或 out of the room，标出从内到外的路径
senses.example: She ran out the door into the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她跑出门，冲进了雨里。
senses.why: The preposition keeps the same crossing but puts a noun after it, so out takes an object and names the opening that is passed through.
senses.whyCN: 介词用法保留同一次越界，只在后面接上名词，于是 out 带宾语，指被穿过的那道出口；词性变了，画面没有变。

intro.en: Out is one of the oldest English adverbs, and its history is a single idea, the far side of a boundary, spreading from place to condition and to fashion.
intro.cn: out 是英语最古老的副词之一，它的历史只有一个念头：边界之外的那一侧；这个念头从位置扩展到状态，再扩展到时尚。

items.en: The root usually reconstructed as ud- carried the sense of outward or upward movement, and it is the deepest layer behind the English word.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构为 ud- 的词根带有「向外、向上」的意思，是英语这个词最深的一层。

items.en: The reconstructed ut gave the Germanic languages an adverb for motion away from the inside.
items.cn: 重构形式 ut 为日耳曼诸语提供了一个表示「离开内部」的副词。

items.en: Old English ut was an adverb of place and direction, and it already appeared beside verbs of going and coming.
items.cn: 古英语 ut 是表示位置与方向的副词，已经常与来去的动词连用。

items.en: Middle English out widened from space to conditions, so a fire or a supply could be called out once it had ended.
items.cn: 中古英语把 out 从空间扩展到状态，火或供应一旦终结就可以说成 out。

items.en: Modern English adds the preposition use, the adjective sense of unfashionable, and a large family of compounds from outset to outlook.
items.cn: 现代英语补上介词用法、表示「过时」的形容词义，以及从 outset 到 outlook 的一大族复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the English out and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers words for the outside position and for leaving.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在英语 out 上的形式，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示外面位置与离开的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a single boundary picture with many uses, so its hooks return to the far side, the step across it, and the state that lies beyond.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是同一个边界画面的多种用法，记忆钩子都回到界外那一侧、跨过去的那一步，以及落在边界之外的状态。

normal.en: Old English ut marked the far side of a boundary, which is why out answers the plain question where.
normal.cn: 古英语 ut 标出边界的那一侧，所以 out 回答最朴素的「在哪里」。

normal.en: The same word covers the crossing as well as the position, so walk and run take it as a direction.
normal.cn: 同一个词既管位置也管越界，所以 walk 与 run 带上它就成了方向。

normal.en: A fire that has left the state of burning is called out, which shows the word moving from space to condition.
normal.cn: 离开燃烧状态的火被叫作 out，显示这个词从空间挪到了状态。

normal.en: Out of date and out of order share one shape: the thing has fallen outside the set of what still works.
normal.cn: out of date 与 out of order 形状相同：东西落到「还能用」的那一套之外了。

normal.en: Outer, outing and outset all keep the boundary picture, and only the part of speech changes.
normal.cn: outer、outing、outset 都保留着边界画面，变的只是词性。

abstract.en: A door standing open with a lamp still burning inside is the word's plainest picture.
abstract.cn: 一扇门开着、屋里灯还亮着，就是这个词最朴素的样子。

abstract.en: A match going dark at the end of a stick is the moment out stops meaning place and starts meaning ended.
abstract.cn: 火柴在棒端熄灭的那一瞬，就是 out 从「位置」转成「结束」的时刻。

abstract.en: A hat left outside a shop window marks a style that has fallen out of favour.

sensesIntro.en: The core is the far side of a boundary; the senses move from that position, to the crossing, to a condition that has ended, to a style outside current taste, and to the preposition of passage.

definition_zh: 喂养；给……吃；喂奶；提供（信息、线索）；饲料；（社交媒体的）动态流
definition_en: to give food to a person, animal or machine, or to supply something such as information; also the food itself or a stream of updates
core_image: 一只摊开的手把食物送进张开的嘴里，链条一样把养分送下去
scene: 傍晚的农场里，父亲提着饲料桶走向鸡舍。 He feeds the chickens before the sun goes down.
sceneCN: 这里 feed 是动词，指「给动物喂食」，对应第 1 个义项；句意为他在太阳落山前喂鸡。

pos.zh: 饲料；一餐；（社交媒体的）动态流

derivatives.zh: 饲养员；喂食器（feed 加施动者后缀 -er，指喂食的人或装置）
喂食；进食（feed 的动名词形式）
反馈（feed 与 back 复合，指信息的回传）

senses.title: To give food to a person or animal
senses.definition: to give food to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或某物食物吃
senses.example: She feeds the baby with a spoon.
senses.exampleCN: 她用勺子喂婴儿。
senses.why: The picture is a hand carrying food to a mouth, so the basic sense is direct giving.
senses.whyCN: 画面是一只手把食物送到嘴边，因此基本义是直接的给予。

senses.title: To eat food
senses.definition: to eat, especially of animals
senses.definitionCN: 吃食物，多用于动物
senses.example: Cows feed on grass.
senses.exampleCN: 牛以草为食。
senses.why: If you can feed someone, the eater can be said to feed as well: the action points both ways.
senses.whyCN: 既然可以喂别人，进食的一方也可以说 feed：动作双向通用。

senses.title: To supply with information or material
senses.definition: to supply a machine, system or person with information, material or power
senses.definitionCN: 给机器、系统或人提供信息、材料或动力
senses.example: The sensors feed data to the computer.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器把数据传给计算机。
senses.why: Food entering a mouth and data entering a system are the same picture: something flows in.
senses.whyCN: 食物入口与数据入系统是同一画面：有东西源源流入。

senses.title: To support or encourage something bad
senses.definition: to make a feeling or situation stronger, especially a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情绪或局面变强，尤指坏的方面
senses.example: Rumours feed public panic.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言助长公众恐慌。
senses.why: A feeling is a mouth too: whatever you feed it, it grows.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也是一张嘴：喂什么，它就长什么。

senses.title: Food for animals
senses.definition: food given to animals
senses.definitionCN: 给动物吃的食物
senses.example: The farmer bought a bag of chicken feed.
senses.exampleCN: 农民买了一袋鸡饲料。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun: the thing given is named after the giving.
senses.whyCN: 动词变名词：被给予之物以「给予」这个动作命名。

senses.title: A stream of updates
senses.definition: a continuous stream of updates or messages, especially online
senses.definitionCN: 持续不断的更新或消息流，多指网络
senses.example: My social media feed is full of cat videos.
senses.exampleCN: 我的社交媒体动态里全是猫的视频。
senses.why: The supply sense meets the internet: content flows to users like feed to animals.
senses.whyCN: 供给义遇上互联网：内容流向用户，就像饲料流向牲口。

intro.en: Feed is an old Germanic strong verb, tied to food and fodder, whose past tense fed has stayed stable for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: feed 是古老的日耳曼强变化动词，与 food、fodder 同源，过去式 fed 一千多年来保持稳定。

items.en: A reconstructed root fodam meant 'food, pasture'; it is the same stock that gives food and fodder.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 fodam 意为「食物、牧场」；food（食物）与 fodder（饲料）同出一源。

items.en: Old English fedan meant 'to nourish, give food to', with past tense fede.
items.cn: 古英语 fedan 意为「滋养、给食」，过去式为 fede。

items.en: Middle English feden kept the strong past form fed and the sense of nourishing people and beasts.
items.cn: 中古英语 feden 保留强变化过去式 fed 及滋养人畜之义。

items.en: Modern English extended feed to machines, data, and feelings, and the noun grew for animal food.
items.cn: 现代英语把 feed 扩展到机器、数据与情绪，名词义指动物饲料。

items.en: The internet age added the news feed, where content streams continuously to users.
items.cn: 互联网时代又添了新闻推送义，内容持续不断地流向用户。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fed shape or the food root; near-meaning words cover giving food and supplying data.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fed 字形或 food 词根；近义组覆盖给食与供数两片义场。

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the food root and the modern data sense.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自 food 词根与现代数据义的记忆抓手。

normal.en: feed and food share the old root: feeding is moving food along.
normal.cn: feed 与 food 同根：喂食就是把食物沿链条传递。

normal.en: The past tense is fed, not feeded: a strong verb that never changed.
normal.cn: 过去式是 fed，不是 feeded：从未变格的强变化动词。

normal.en: feed on means what an animal lives on, as cows feed on grass.
normal.cn: feed on 指动物以何为食，如牛吃草。

normal.en: feedback is information fed back to the source, one of the oldest loan ideas from engineering.
normal.cn: feedback 是把信息回传给源头，工程学传来的经典概念。

normal.en: A news feed keeps dropping content into your day, like a bucket that never empties.
normal.cn: 新闻推送不断往你一天里投放内容，像一个倒不空的桶。

abstract.en: Every feed is a pipe: whatever flows in, something grows at the far end.
abstract.cn: 每次喂送都是一条管道：流入什么，末端就长出什么。

abstract.en: Attention is the mouth of the mind; the feed decides the diet.
abstract.cn: 注意力是心灵之口，信息流决定精神食谱。

abstract.en: To feed a rumour is to water a weed: it grows overnight.
abstract.cn: 喂谣言如同给野草浇水：一夜疯长。

examples.en: The nurse feeds the patients who cannot move their hands.
examples.cn: 护士给不能动手的病人喂饭。

examples.en: The software feeds live prices to the trading system.
examples.cn: 软件向交易系统提供实时价格。

examples.en: Farmers store enough feed for the winter months.
examples.cn: 农民储备足够的饲料过冬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费的」—— 买饲料是要花钱（费）的，花了钱才能喂 → feed 喂养、饲料

root: 与 food、fodder 同出日耳曼语根（重构形式 fodam，一般认为表「食物」），经古英语 fedan「滋养」而来；核心是「把食物送下去」。

sensesIntro.en: From giving food outward to eating, supplying systems, fuelling feelings, animal food, and online streams.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「给食」扩展到进食、为系统供数、助长情绪、动物饲料与网络信息流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand carrying food down an open mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手把食物送进张开的嘴。

branches.en: GIVING: putting food into a mouth.
branches.cn: 给予：把食物送进嘴里。

branches.en: EATING: the receiving end of the same action.
branches.cn: 进食：同一动作的接收端。

branches.en: SUPPLY: feeding systems with data or power.
branches.cn: 供给：为系统提供数据或动力。

branches.en: MATERIAL: the food itself, for animals or machines.
branches.cn: 物料：食物本身，用于牲口或机器。

branches.en: THE STREAM: continuous content flowing to users.
branches.cn: 信息流：持续流向用户的内容。

intro.en: Feed forms compounds faster than affixes; the family lives on food words and data words.
intro.cn: feed 更多以复合构词见长；词族分布在食物词与数据词两端。

latinIntro.en: Feed is Germanic to the core; Latin used entirely different words for feeding, so there are no Latin siblings.
latinIntro.cn: feed 是纯正的日耳曼词；拉丁语用完全不同的词表喂食，因此没有拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: one who or that which feeds

items.exampleCN: 树上挂着一个鸟类喂食器。

items.meaning: food for chickens; a tiny sum

definition_zh: 方法；办法；条理；体系；（学科或艺术的）方法论体系
definition_en: a particular way of doing something, especially one that is planned and systematic, or the order and system that such a way produces
core_image: 一条被反复踩出的小路：草被踩平了，路指向远处的目标
scene: 老实验室里的那套流程几十年没有变过。 The lab still uses a method that has not changed in forty years.
sceneCN: 这里 method 是「方法」（第 1 个义项：做某事的特定程序）；句意：这个实验室仍在使用一套四十年没变过的方法。场景要点：一排贴着编号的旧仪器、墙上手写的步骤表、被踩得发亮的地面；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.phrase: there is method in one's madness

senses.title: A way of doing something
senses.titleCN: 方法：做某事的特定路数
senses.definition: a particular procedure for doing something, especially a planned and systematic one
senses.definitionCN: 做某事的特定程序，尤指有计划、有系统的程序
senses.example: The lab still uses a method that has not changed in forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验室仍在使用一套四十年没变过的方法。
senses.why: Method reached English in the early 15th century from Greek methodos, originally 'pursuit, a following after'. A method is a path that has already been walked and can be walked again.
senses.whyCN: method 于 15 世纪初从希腊语 methodos 进入英语，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。方法就是一条已经被人走过、还可以再走一遍的路。

senses.title: Orderliness
senses.definition: the quality of acting in an orderly, systematic way rather than at random
senses.definitionCN: 做事有条理、有系统，而非随意的品质
senses.example: There was method in the way she sorted the files, though no one else could see it.
senses.exampleCN: 她整理文件的方式自有章法，只是别人看不出来。
senses.why: From the 1610s the word also named 'orderliness, regularity'. The path is no longer a particular route but the habit of always walking on one.
senses.whyCN: 自 17 世纪 10 年代起，这个词也指“有条理、有规律”。此时路不再是一条具体路线，而是“总要沿着某条路走”的习惯。

senses.title: A complete system
senses.definition: a complete set of rules or procedures for attaining an end
senses.definitionCN: 为达到某一目的而设的一整套规则或程序
senses.example: The school adopted a new method for teaching reading.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采用了一套新的阅读教学体系。
senses.why: The sense 'a system or complete set of rules' is recorded from the 1680s. Once a path is written down as rules, it can be taught to strangers.
senses.whyCN: “体系或完整规则集”这一义项自 17 世纪 80 年代有记录。一旦一条路被写成规则，它就能教给陌生人。

senses.title: Scientific method
senses.titleCN: 科学方法：学科自己的路
senses.definition: the established procedure of a discipline for testing claims and producing knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科为检验主张、生产知识而确立的程序
senses.example: The scientific method is less a single recipe than a set of habits of doubt.
senses.exampleCN: 科学方法与其说是一份单一配方，不如说是一组怀疑的习惯。
senses.why: Greek methodos already meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry'. Science did not invent the word; it inherited the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 methodos 本就意为“科学探究、探究的方法”。科学没有发明这个词，它继承的是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Teaching and acting methods
senses.titleCN: 教学法与表演体系：一门手艺的路
senses.definition: a named system of practice in teaching or in the arts, such as the direct method or method acting
senses.definitionCN: 教学或艺术中以人名或特征命名的实践体系，如直接教学法、方法派表演
senses.example: Method acting asks the performer to draw on real memories.
senses.exampleCN: 方法派表演要求演员调动真实的记忆。
senses.why: A system with a name becomes a school. Method here is a path that a whole profession agrees to walk together.
senses.whyCN: 一套有名字的体系会变成一派。这里的 method 是一整门行业同意一起走的那条路。

senses.title: Old medical sense
senses.titleCN: 医学旧义：系统化的治疗方案
senses.definition: in early use, the regular, systematic treatment of disease
senses.definitionCN: 在早期用法中，指对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗
senses.example: The medieval physician spoke of a method for fevers, not a single remedy.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的医生讲的是治疗热病的一套方法，而不是某一味药。
senses.why: The first English sense, in the early 15th century, was 'regular, systematic treatment of disease'. The word entered through medicine before it belonged to everything else.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的第一个义项是 15 世纪初的“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”。这个词先通过医学进来，然后才属于一切别的事物。

senses.title: Method in programming
senses.titleCN: 编程中的方法：对象身上的函数
senses.definition: in object-oriented programming, a function or procedure attached to an object or class
senses.definitionCN: 在面向对象编程中，附着于对象或类上的函数或过程
senses.example: The method returns a new list instead of changing the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法返回一个新列表，而不修改旧列表。
senses.why: The metaphor survives in code: a method is still a fixed route the object knows how to take when it is called.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在代码里活了下来：方法仍是对象被调用时知道该怎么走的一条固定路线。

senses.title: A method of inquiry
senses.titleCN: 探究之路：哲学意义上的方法
senses.definition: in philosophy, the deliberate path of doubt or reasoning by which a conclusion is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，为抵达结论而有意采取的怀疑或推理之路
senses.example: Descartes began with a method of doubt that would leave only certainty standing.
senses.exampleCN: 笛卡尔从一种怀疑的方法开始，只为留下确定的东西。
senses.why: Methodos was literally a following after something. Philosophy turns that pursuit into a rule for how to pursue anything at all.
senses.whyCN: methodos 字面上就是“跟在某物之后追”。哲学把这趟追寻变成一条规则，规定该怎样追寻任何东西。

senses.title: Method in one's madness
senses.definition: in the phrase 'there is method in one's madness', used when apparently foolish behaviour turns out to have a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 「there is method in one's madness」 中，指看似荒唐的行为其实自有目的
senses.example: He shuffles the cards for ten minutes, but there is method in his madness.
senses.exampleCN: 他把牌洗了十分钟，看似荒唐，其实自有章法。
senses.why: Shakespeare's phrase 'though this be madness, yet there is method in it' (Hamlet) gave English a fixed way to say that a path is hidden inside chaos.
senses.whyCN: 莎士比亚的句子“though this be madness, yet there is method in it”（《哈姆雷特》）给了英语一个固定说法：混乱里藏着一条路。

intro.en: Method is Greek: meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road, way'. Latin borrowed it as methodus and passed it to French and English. It has no connection with medical, despite the shared -met- shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: method 是希腊词：meta“追寻”加 hodos“路、道”。拉丁语把它借作 methodus，再传给法语和英语。尽管有共同的 -met- 外形，它与 medical 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'regular, systematic treatment of disease', through Latin methodus 'way of teaching or going' and Greek methodos.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 15 世纪初，意为“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”，经拉丁语 methodus“教学或行走之道”与希腊语 methodos 而来。

items.en: Greek methodos meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry, investigation', and originally 'pursuit, a following after'.
items.cn: 希腊语 methodos 意为“科学探究、探究的方法、调查”，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。

items.en: The word joins meta 'in pursuit or quest of' and hodos 'a way, path, track, road', also 'a journey'. Hodos is of uncertain origin; Beekes suggests PIE *sod- 'course', and it is traditionally linked to Slavic words for 'course'.
items.cn: 这个词由 meta“追寻、求索”与 hodos“路、路径、轨道、道路”（也指“旅程”）组合而成。hodos 的来源不确定；Beekes 提出原始印欧语 *sod-“行程”，传统上也把它与斯拉夫语表示“行程”的词联系起来。

items.en: The sense widened to 'any way of doing anything' in the 1580s, to 'orderliness, regularity' in the 1610s, and to 'a system or complete set of rules' in the 1680s.
items.cn: 词义在 16 世纪 80 年代扩展到“做任何事的方式”，17 世纪 10 年代扩展到“有条理、有规律”，17 世纪 80 年代扩展到“体系或完整的一套规则”。

items.en: The phrase method acting is recorded in reference to the theory associated with the Russian director Konstantin Stanislavski.
items.cn: method acting 这一说法有记录，指与俄国导演康斯坦丁·斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基相关的理论。

items.en: Medical goes back to Latin medicus 'physician', with no Greek element. Meta- in method is the Greek preposition 'in pursuit of', not the modern prefix meaning 'beyond' or 'after'; the two words only share letters.
items.cn: medical 追溯到拉丁语 medicus“医生”，不含希腊语成分。method 里的 meta- 是希腊语介词“追寻”，不是现代表示“超越、之后”的前缀；两个词只共享字母。

note.en: The first group is the word family built on method: the adjective, the adverb and the study of method. The second group compares the nouns English uses for 'a way of doing something', which differ in scale and in who owns the way.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 method 上的词族：形容词、副词与研究方法的学问。第二组比较英语里表示“做某事的方式”的几个名词，区别在于尺度大小与“这条路归谁”。

entries.definition: the branch of knowledge that studies methods, or the set of methods used in a field. It is not a longer synonym of method: a methodology can contain several methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究方法的学问分支，或某一领域所使用的一套方法。它不是 method 的加长同义词：一套方法论里可以包含好几种方法。

entries.definition: done according to a method; orderly and systematic. It describes a person or a procedure, not a route.
entries.definitionCN: 按方法进行的；有条理、有系统的。它描述人或程序，而不描述一条路线。

entries.definition: in an orderly, step-by-step way. It answers 'how', while method answers 'by what route'.
entries.definitionCN: 有条理地、一步一步地。它回答“怎样做”，而 method 回答“走哪条路”。

entries.definition: to reduce something to order or system. The verb turns the noun into an action; it is rare outside formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物整理成秩序或体系。这个动词把名词变成动作；在正式写作之外很少见。

entries.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or subject, often including the attitude behind it. It is broader and softer than method, which implies explicit steps.
entries.definitionCN: 处理问题或课题的方式，常包含背后的态度。它比 method 更宽、更软，而 method 暗示明确的步骤。

entries.definition: a particular way of carrying out a single task, especially one requiring skill. Techniques are the small parts inside a method.
entries.definitionCN: 完成单项任务的具体方式，尤指需要技巧的那种。technique 是 method 内部的一个个小零件。

entries.definition: a thing or resource used to achieve an end. Means answers 'with what'; method answers 'in what order'.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而使用的东西或资源。means 回答“用什么”，method 回答“按什么顺序”。

entries.definition: an established or official sequence of steps. It is more bureaucratic than method and often written down by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的或官方的步骤顺序。它比 method 更带行政色彩，常由某个权威写下来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road', the Latin borrowing methodus, and the family methodical, methodology, methodize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”、拉丁语借词 methodus，以及 methodical、methodology、methodize 词族。

normal.en: hodos means 'road'. A method is literally 'a following after on a road': meta plus hodos.
normal.cn: hodos 意为“路”。method 字面上就是“沿路跟随”：meta 加 hodos。

normal.en: In method, meta- does not mean 'beyond' or 'after' as it does in modern English; it means 'in pursuit of'. The Greek preposition is about chasing, not about position.
normal.cn: 在 method 里，meta- 不像现代英语那样表示“超越”或“之后”，而是“追寻”。这个希腊语介词讲的是追赶，不是位置。

normal.en: Methodology is not a fancy word for method: it is the study of methods, or the whole set of them used in a field.
normal.cn: methodology 不是 method 的高级说法：它是对方法的研究，或某一领域所使用的整套方法。

normal.en: Methodical describes the person who always walks on a path; method names the path itself.
normal.cn: methodical 描述那个总沿着路走的人；method 命名的是那条路本身。

normal.en: Medical looks similar but is Latin medicus 'physician'. One word has a road in it, the other has a doctor.
normal.cn: medical 看着像，其实是拉丁语 medicus“医生”。一个词里装着一条路，另一个词里装着一位医生。

abstract.en: Picture grass in a field. One path is visible because many feet chose the same line; that line is a method.
abstract.cn: 想象一片草地。有一条路看得见，是因为许多脚选择了同一条线；那条线就是 method。

abstract.en: A path can be walked by one person or written down for a school. The moment it is written down, method becomes methodology.
abstract.cn: 一条路可以由一个人走，也可以写下来给一个学派。写下来的那一刻，method 就变成了 methodology。

abstract.en: Method is the order of steps, not the tool in your hand. A hammer is a means; how you swing it is a technique; the sequence is the method.
abstract.cn: method 是步骤的顺序，不是你手里的工具。锤子是 means；怎么挥是 technique；先后次序才是 method。

examples.en: No method will save a study that was badly designed in the first place.
examples.cn: 如果一项研究一开始就设计得很糟，任何方法都救不了它。

examples.en: She works without method, yet somehow finishes before everyone else.
examples.cn: 她做事毫无章法，却总能比别人先做完。

examples.en: The two laboratories use different methods and keep getting different numbers.
examples.cn: 两个实验室用不同的方法，得到的数字也一直不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卖瑟德”——卖瑟德把一条踩出来的小路画在纸上，卖给后来的人照着走 → method 方法、办法（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自希腊语 methodos“追寻、探究”，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，核心是“沿着一条路追到目标”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of method, all from one image: a line worn into the grass by feet that wanted the same destination. It can be one path, the habit of taking paths, or the written map of them.
sensesIntro.cn: method 的九个义项都来自同一幅画面：一条被想抵达同一目标的脚踩出来的草径。它可以是某一条路、走路的习惯，或被写下来的路线图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path worn into grass, pointing at a destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被踩进草地的小路，指向某个目的地。

branches.en: THE PATH: the oldest senses name a procedure, first for curing disease, then for anything at all.
branches.cn: 路：最老的义项命名一套程序，先用于治病，后用于任何事。

branches.en: THE HABIT: orderliness is walking on a path by choice, and the idiom says a path may hide inside apparent chaos.
branches.cn: 习惯：条理是有意识地沿路走；那条习语则说，混乱里也可能藏着一条路。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: written rules turn a path into a teachable system, and science inherits the oldest 'inquiry' sense.
branches.cn: 体系：写下来的规则把路变成可教的体系，而科学继承的是最古老的“探究”义。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: teaching and acting give the path a proper name, and philosophy makes the pursuit itself a rule.
branches.cn: 学派：教学与表演给这条路一个专名，哲学则把追寻本身变成规则。

branches.en: THE CODE: in software the object still knows a fixed route to take when called.
branches.cn: 代码：在软件里，对象被调用时仍知道该走哪条固定路线。

intro.en: Method is a Greek compound borrowed whole: meta- plus hodos 'road'. English adds -ical, -ically, -ology, -ologist and -ize, while the same hodos builds episode, period and Exodus.
intro.cn: method 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：meta- 加 hodos“路”。英语加上 -ical、-ically、-ology、-ologist、-ize，而同一个 hodos 还构成 episode、period、Exodus。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek word unchanged as methodus 'way of teaching or going', and Late Latin methodicus came from Greek methodikos. Latin had its own word for 'way', modus, but method did not come from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样吸收希腊词作 methodus“教学或行走之道”，晚期拉丁语 methodicus 来自希腊语 methodikos。拉丁语自己表示“方式”的词是 modus，但 method 并非来自它。

items.meaning: a following after on a road; a way of doing something
items.meaningCN: 沿路追寻；做某事的方法（meta- 追寻 + hodos 路）
items.example: They tried every method and failed with each.
items.exampleCN: 他们试了每一种方法，每一种都失败了。

items.meaningCN: 按方法进行的；有条理的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: His methodical notes filled four notebooks.
items.exampleCN: 他条理分明的笔记写满了四个本子。

items.meaningCN: 有条理地；一步一步地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 她逐个抽屉有条理地检查。

items.meaning: the study of methods; a set of methods used in a field
items.meaningCN: 方法论；一套研究方法（-ology 表学问）
items.example: The paper was rejected for its weak methodology.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文因方法论薄弱而被拒。

items.example: The two studies differ on methodological grounds.
items.exampleCN: 这两项研究在方法上存在分歧。

items.meaning: a specialist in methods of research
items.example: A methodologist was added to the review panel.
items.exampleCN: 评审组里增加了一位方法论专家。

items.meaning: to arrange according to a system
items.meaningCN: 使有条理；使系统化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: He methodized the archive over one winter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一个冬天把档案整理成体系。

items.meaning: a member of the Protestant denomination founded at Oxford in 1729
items.meaningCN: 卫理公会教徒（-ist 表追随者，源于其讲究方法的修行方式）
items.example: The Methodist chapel still stands on the corner.
items.exampleCN: 卫理公会礼拜堂仍立在街角。

items.structure: epi- (besides) + eisodos (a coming in, from hodos 'way')
items.meaning: an incident or instalment inserted into a larger whole
items.meaningCN: 插曲；（系列中的）一集（epi- 另外 + eisodos 进入，含 hodos 路）
items.exampleCN: 最后一集什么也没解答。

items.meaning: a going round; a length of time
items.meaningCN: 周期；一段时间（peri- 环绕 + hodos 路，即“绕一圈”）
items.example: The period lasted almost a century.
items.exampleCN: 这一时期持续了将近一个世纪。

items.meaning: a going out; a mass departure
items.meaningCN: 出走；大批离去（ex- 向外 + hodos 路）
items.example: The drought set off an exodus from the villages.
items.exampleCN: 旱灾引发了村庄的大批出走。

items.meaning: a performance technique that draws on the actor's own experience
items.meaningCN: 方法派表演（以体系命名的表演技术）
items.example: Method acting changed how American films were shot.

definition_zh: 每个人；人人；大家
definition_en: every person; all people
core_image: 热闹的操场：上课铃一响，所有人都跑回教室
scene: 大扫除一开始，教室里人人都动了起来。 Everybody helped to clean the classroom after school.
sceneCN: 这里 everybody 是「每个人」（第 1 个义项：所有人无一例外）；句意是放学后大家都帮忙打扫教室。

derivatives.zh: 同义代词，语体稍正式
由 every 加 thing 构成，指物，义为「一切」
基础词，古义可指「人」，义为「身体」

senses.title: Every person, all people
senses.definition: every single person in a group, followed by a singular verb
senses.definitionCN: 一群中的每一个人，后接单数动词
senses.example: Everybody was happy with the picnic plan.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人对野餐计划都很满意。
senses.why: The word joins every with body, an old word for a person, then ticks each name and counts the whole.
senses.whyCN: 该词由 every 与 body（古义指人）结合，先逐个点名再合为一体。

senses.title: People in general
senses.definition: people in general, often in friendly spoken phrases
senses.definitionCN: 泛指一般人，常见于亲切的口语表达
senses.example: Everybody loves a sunny holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 人人都爱阳光灿烂的假期。
senses.why: When the group is left unnamed, the roll call stretches out to cover all people.
senses.whyCN: 当群体未指明时，点名册扩展覆盖所有人。

intro.en: Everybody fuses every with body, which in older English could simply mean a person. It has kept its friendly, spoken tone ever since.
intro.cn: everybody 由 every 与 body 融合，body 在古英语可单指「人」。该词一直保留亲切的口语色彩。

items.en: Old English bodig meant the physical body, but body could also stand for a person.
items.cn: 古英语 bodig 指身体，但 body 也可指代一个人。

items.en: The compound everybody formed beside everyone in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十四世纪复合词 everybody 与 everyone 并肩形成。

items.en: It took the friendly spoken role, while everyone leaned more formal.
items.cn: 它承担口语亲切角色，everyone 则偏正式。

items.en: Grammar settled the singular verb: everybody is, not everybody are.
items.cn: 语法确定单数动词：everybody is 而非 everybody are。

items.en: The singular their, as in everybody brought their lunch, is now widely accepted.
items.cn: 单数配复数 their（如 everybody brought their lunch）如今已被广泛接受。

note.en: The first group collects the every-compound family; the second collects near meanings about people.
note.cn: 第一组收集 every 复合词族；第二组收集与「人」相关的近义词。

entries.definitionCN: 每个人。意义相同，语气稍正式。

entries.definition: all the other people besides the one mentioned
entries.definitionCN: 其他所有人。加 else 排除所提之人。

entries.definition: some person unknown, used in positive sentences
entries.definitionCN: 某人。用于肯定句，指不确定的某人。

entries.definition: a close synonym, interchangeable in most sentences
entries.definitionCN: 每个人。最接近的同义词，多数句子可互换。

entries.definition: the whole group, takes plural verbs
entries.definitionCN: 全部；所有人。接复数动词。

entries.definition: any person at all, often in questions and negatives
entries.definitionCN: 任何人。常用于疑问句与否定句。

normalIntro.cn: 五条基于 body 词根与校园场景的具体联想。

normal.en: Everybody plus body: each body, each person, is present.
normal.cn: everybody＝every＋body：每个「body（人）」都在场。

normal.en: Everybody is here takes the singular verb is, not are.
normal.cn: Everybody is here 用单数动词 is，语法别丢。

normal.en: Everybody sounds friendlier than everyone in chat.
normal.cn: everybody 比 everyone 更口语，聊天时更常用。

normal.en: Everybody knows is a high-frequency line in songs and talk.
normal.cn: Everybody knows 是歌词和口语里的高频句。

normal.en: The sound hints at wanting to hug each person, for spelling only.
normal.cn: 谐音：「爱夫瑞抱低」——想抱一抱每个人，帮助拼读，不是词源。

abstract.en: Picture the whole playground emptying into classrooms at the bell.
abstract.cn: 画面：铃响时整个操场的人都跑回教室。

abstract.en: See every hand go up at the same time.
abstract.cn: 动作：全班的手同时举起。

abstract.en: Feel one big circle of arms around the whole group.
abstract.cn: 感觉：一个大圈的手臂围住全组。

examples.en: Everybody was excited about the sports day.
examples.cn: 大家都为运动会感到兴奋。

examples.en: Come on, everybody, it is time to go home.
examples.cn: 来吧大家，该回家了。

examples.en: Almost everybody in our class likes this song.
examples.cn: 我们班几乎每个人都喜欢这首歌。

sensesIntro.en: Everybody counts every person one by one, then gathers them into one friendly, spoken whole.
sensesIntro.cn: everybody 先逐人清点，再以亲切的口吻合为全体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the whole playground pouring back into classrooms at the bell.
core.cn: 核心意象：铃响时整个操场的人都涌回教室。

intro.cn: everybody 由 every 复合 body；同辈为 everyone、everything 与 everywhere。

definition_zh: 电；电力；电荷；电学；强烈的兴奋感
definition_en: the physical effect of electric charge, the power supplied through wires, or a tense feeling of excitement
core_image: 看不见的电流在铜线里奔跑，一按开关，整间屋子的灯同时亮起
scene: 雷雨夜里，整条街的灯忽然同时熄灭，只有远处的闪电把屋顶照白。 When the storm cut the electricity, the whole street went dark at once.
sceneCN: 这里 electricity 指「送入住户与街道的电力供应」（第 4 个义项：供电、用电）；句意为暴风雨切断供电时，整条街同时黑了。图中可辨识物件：闪电、熄灭的路灯、窗户里的烛光、雨幕。

pos.zh: 兴奋的情绪张力；强烈的活力（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 电的；电动的；令人激动的
电气的；与电有关的
电工
使带电；使震惊
电气化
电子学；电子器件

senses.title: The physical phenomenon
senses.titleCN: 电：电荷及其效应这一物理现象
senses.definition: the physical phenomenon of electric charge, its movement and its effects
senses.definitionCN: 电荷及其运动与效应构成的物理现象
senses.example: Electricity is easiest to see when it jumps across a gap as a spark.
senses.exampleCN: 电最容易看见的时候，是它作为火花跳过一道缝隙。
senses.why: The word names an invisible event that becomes visible only at its edge, which is why early students spoke of a fluid.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是看不见的事件，只在边缘才现形，因此早期研究者把它说成一种流体。

senses.title: Power sold as energy
senses.titleCN: 电能、电力：作为能源使用的电
senses.definition: electric power treated as a form of energy that can be generated and sold
senses.definitionCN: 把电当作可以生产、出售的一种能源
senses.example: The plant sells electricity to three neighbouring towns.
senses.exampleCN: 这座电厂向邻近的三个镇供电。
senses.why: Once electricity could be metered and billed, the phenomenon turned into a commodity measured in units.
senses.whyCN: 当电能被计量、收费，这个现象就变成了以单位计价的商品。

senses.title: Charge carried by particles
senses.definition: the electric charge that particles carry and transfer
senses.definitionCN: 粒子携带与转移的电荷
senses.example: Rubbing the rod transfers electricity to the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 摩擦棒子把电荷转移到布上。
senses.why: The word can point at the quantity itself rather than at the effect, especially when it moves from one body to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指向那个量本身，而不是效应，尤其当它从一个物体转到另一个物体时。

senses.title: The supply to a building
senses.titleCN: 供电、用电：送到房屋或街道的电
senses.definition: the supply of electric power to a building, a street or a region
senses.definitionCN: 向房屋、街道或地区输送的电力
senses.example: When the storm cut the electricity, the whole street went dark at once.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨切断供电时，整条街同时黑了。
senses.why: In daily speech people say the electricity for the service they buy, not for the physics behind it.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语里，人们用这个词指自己买到的服务，而不是背后的物理原理。

senses.title: Charge that stays put
senses.titleCN: 静电：停留在物体上的电荷
senses.definition: charge that gathers on an object and stays there until it is discharged
senses.definitionCN: 聚集在物体上、直到被释放才消失的电荷
senses.example: Walking across the carpet built up enough electricity to make a spark.
senses.exampleCN: 走过地毯积起的静电足以打出一个火花。
senses.why: A stored charge has no circuit to flow through, so it sits still and surprises the hand that touches it.
senses.whyCN: 被储存的电荷没有回路可走，于是停在原处，吓到伸手去碰的人。

senses.title: The branch of physics
senses.titleCN: 电学：研究电荷的物理分支
senses.definition: the branch of physics that studies electric charge, current and related effects
senses.definitionCN: 研究电荷、电流及相关效应的物理分支
senses.example: He studied electricity before switching to acoustics.
senses.exampleCN: 他先学电学，后来转去研究声学。
senses.why: A phenomenon with laws and instruments turns into a subject taught under its own name.
senses.whyCN: 一个有定律、有仪器的现象，会变成以自己名字授课的学科。

senses.title: Tension in a room
senses.titleCN: 情绪张力：现场紧张而兴奋的气氛
senses.definition: a tense, exciting feeling that seems to fill a room or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 似乎充满房间或表演现场的紧张兴奋感
senses.example: The electricity in the hall rose as the band took the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队登台时，礼堂里的紧张感一下子升高了。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the spark: something invisible passes between people and makes the air feel charged.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了火花：某种看不见的东西在人与人之间传递，让空气像带了电。

senses.title: Energy in a place
senses.titleCN: 抽象活力：让地方振作起来的劲头
senses.definition: a feeling of energy and excitement that spreads through a place or a group
senses.definitionCN: 在一个地方或群体中扩散开来的活力与兴奋
senses.example: The new plan brought electricity to a tired neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 新方案给一个疲惫的社区带来了生气。
senses.why: The abstract sense widens the charge from a room to a whole district, where the current is social rather than electrical.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把电荷从一间屋子扩展到整个街区，那里的电流是社会的，而不是电学的。

intro.en: Electricity was coined in the seventeenth century on the Greek word for amber, the substance that first showed the effect. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: electricity 于十七世纪用希腊语中「琥珀」一词造出，琥珀正是最早显现这一效应的物质。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek ēlektron meant amber, and rubbed amber was known to attract light objects such as straw and feathers. The deeper origin of the Greek word is source uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 ēlektron 意为琥珀，人们早已知道摩擦过的琥珀能吸引草屑、羽毛等轻物。这个希腊词更深层的来源属于来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as electrum, which named both amber and a pale gold alloy; English took the same stem through learned Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该希腊名词作 electrum，既指琥珀，也指一种淡金色的合金；英语经学术拉丁语继承了同一词干。

items.en: William Gilbert coined electricus around 1600 for substances that behave like rubbed amber, using the Latin stem rather than the Greek one.
items.cn: 吉尔伯特约在 1600 年造出 electricus，指行为像摩擦琥珀的物质，用的是拉丁词干而非希腊词干。

items.en: English electric appears in the seventeenth century as the adjective for that attracting power, and electricity follows as its noun.
items.cn: 英语 electric 在十七世纪出现，用作这种吸引力的形容词，随后 electricity 作为名词跟上。

items.en: Sir Thomas Browne is often credited with the first English use of electricity in the 1640s; the exact date is approximate and the spelling varied.
items.cn: 人们常把 electricity 最早的英语使用归给托马斯·布朗，时在十七世纪四十年代；确切年代只是约数，拼写也多有变化。

items.en: Nineteenth-century generators turned electricity into a public supply, and twentieth-century writing extended the word to the excitement felt in a crowd.
items.cn: 十九世纪的发电机把电变成公共供应，二十世纪的写作又把这个词扩展到人群中的兴奋感。

note.en: Group one holds relatives and look-alikes of the electric stem; group two holds the physical quantities people mix it up with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 electric 词干的亲属词与形近词；第二组是常被与它混淆的物理量。

entries.definition: Describes a device or effect that works by electricity; electricity is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容靠电工作的装置或效应；electricity 是对应名词。

entries.definition: The broader adjective for systems and engineering, not for a single working device.
entries.definitionCN: 更广的形容词，用于系统与工程，而非单台工作装置。

entries.definition: The negatively charged particle; electricity is the flow or effect of such particles.
entries.definitionCN: 带负电的粒子；electricity 是这些粒子的流动或效应。

entries.definition: A person who installs and repairs wiring; the ending -ian marks a trade.
entries.definitionCN: 安装与维修线路的人；-ian 后缀标记职业。

entries.definition: The general word for energy delivered to homes, measured in watts; electricity is one form of it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指送到住户的能量，以瓦计量；electricity 是其中一种形式。

entries.definition: The rate at which charge moves through a wire; it is the flow, not the supply.
entries.definitionCN: 电荷在导线中移动的速率；指流动，而非供应。

entries.definition: The amount of electricity a body carries, measured in coulombs.
entries.definitionCN: 物体所带电的量，以库仑计量。

entries.definition: The capacity to do work in any form; electricity is only one carrier of it.
entries.definitionCN: 任何形式的做功能力；电只是它的一种载体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek source, the real derivatives and the real phrases of the electricity family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊语来源、真实的派生词，以及电这个词族里真实的搭配。

normal.en: The word began with amber: rubbed amber pulled straw, and the effect was named after the stuff.
normal.cn: 这个词从琥珀开始：摩擦过的琥珀能吸草屑，效应就以这种材料命名。

normal.en: The family runs electric, electrical, electrician, electrify, electrification and electronics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 electric、electrical、electrician、electrify、electrification 与 electronics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the supply sense: generate electricity, electricity supply, electricity bill.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出供应义：发电、电力供应、电费账单。

normal.en: The adjective and the noun split the work: electric device, electrical system, electricity supply.
normal.cn: 形容词与名词分工：电动的装置、电气的系统、电力的供应。

normal.en: Static electricity is charge with nowhere to go, which is why it waits and then shocks.
normal.cn: 静电是无处可去的电荷，因此它先等在那里，然后电你一下。

abstract.en: Picture water in a pipe: the pressure is voltage, the flow is current, and the water itself is charge.
abstract.cn: 想象水管里的水：水压是电压，水流是电流，水本身是电荷。

abstract.en: Picture a spark as the moment the invisible becomes visible.
abstract.cn: 想象火花就是看不见的东西现形的那一瞬。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone speaks at once and the air itself seems to hum.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人同时开口，连空气都像在嗡嗡作响。

examples.en: The village lived without electricity for a week after the line came down.
examples.cn: 线路倒下之后，村子过了一周没有电的日子。

examples.en: Copper wire carries electricity better than iron does.
examples.cn: 铜线导电比铁好。

examples.en: There was electricity in the room when the two rivals finally met.
examples.cn: 两个对手终于见面时，屋里充满了紧张的气氛。

dict_mnemonic.text: electr-（琥珀）+ -icity（性质、状态）——摩擦琥珀吸起草屑的那种性质 → 电；供电

root: 希腊 ēlektron（琥珀）→ 拉丁 electrum → 新拉丁 electricus（吉尔伯特，约 1600）→ 英语 electric → electricity。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from an invisible physical event to a commodity, a quantity, a household service, a stored charge, a science, and finally to the excitement in a room and in a district.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从看不见的物理事件走到商品、数量、住户服务、储存的电荷、一门学科，最后落到房间与街区里的兴奋感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible current running through copper, switching a whole building into light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股看不见的电流在铜线里奔跑，把整栋楼点亮。

branches.en: The phenomenon and the quantity: what happens, and how much of it a body carries.
branches.cn: 现象与数量：发生了什么，以及物体带了多少。

branches.en: The commodity and the household service it becomes once it is metered.
branches.cn: 商品与住户服务：一旦被计量，它就变成这两样东西。

branches.en: Charge that cannot move, waiting on a surface to surprise the next hand.
branches.cn: 不能移动的电荷，停在表面等着吓到下一只手。

branches.en: The effects made into a subject with laws, instruments and textbooks.
branches.cn: 把种种效应变成一门有定律、仪器与教科书的学科。

branches.en: The spark detached from wires and felt as tension in a room or energy in a district.
branches.cn: 火花脱离导线，被感受为屋里的紧张或街区的生气。

intro.en: Electricity is a noun on the electric stem with -ity, and the whole family reads from the Greek word for amber.
intro.cn: electricity 是 electric 词干加 -ity 构成的名词，整个词族都可以从希腊语「琥珀」读起。

latinIntro.en: Greek ēlektron gave Latin electrum, and New Latin electricus supplied the stem on which English built every derivative.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 ēlektron 给出拉丁 electrum，新拉丁 electricus 提供词干，英语在其上构造了全部派生词。

items.meaningCN: 电的；电动的（加形容词后缀，材料名转为性质）
items.example: An electric pump drained the cellar.
items.exampleCN: 一台电动泵把地窖的水抽干。

items.meaning: the state or effect of electric charge
items.meaningCN: 电；电力（加性质后缀，形容词转为抽象名词）
电气的；与电有关的（再加形容词后缀，范围由单台设备扩到系统）

items.meaning: a person who installs and repairs electric systems
items.meaningCN: 电工（加人名词后缀，性质转为职业）
items.exampleCN: 一名电工检测了配电盘。

items.meaning: to charge with electricity; to shock
items.meaningCN: 使带电；使震惊（加使动后缀，名词变动词并引申为震惊）
items.example: The fence is electrified at night.

items.meaning: the process of bringing electricity to a place
items.meaningCN: 电气化（再加过程后缀，动作转为大规模工程）

items.meaning: the study and use of electronic devices
items.meaningCN: 电子学；电子器件（由电子加学科后缀，粒子转成技术领域）
静电的（由「电」与「静止」复合，流动义被取消）
水电的（由「水」与「电」复合，动力来源变成水流）
items.example: The hydroelectric dam feeds the grid.

latinEntries.structure: electricus, electrica, electricum (New Latin adjective, c. 1600)

definition_zh: 勇敢的；无所畏惧的；需要勇气的；勇敢面对（危险）；壮丽的（书面）
definition_en: ready to face danger, pain or difficulty without fear, and to go out and meet such danger, or (in old use) fine and splendid
core_image: 大风里仍向前迈步、不肯后退的人
scene: 悬崖边，少年顶着风把被困的小狗抱了回来。 The brave boy carried the trapped dog back from the cliff.
sceneCN: 这里 brave 是「勇敢的」（第 1 个义项：面对危险不退缩）；句意为那个勇敢的男孩把被困的小狗从悬崖边抱了回来。

pos.zh: 形容词：勇敢的；无所畏惧的；壮丽的
动词：勇敢面对；冒着（危险、恶劣天气）

derivatives.zh: 由 brave 加 -ery 构成，义为「勇敢；勇气」

senses.title: Ready to face danger
senses.definition: ready to face danger, pain or difficulty without fear
senses.definitionCN: 面对危险、痛苦或困难而不畏惧
senses.example: The brave girl saved the cat from the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那个勇敢的女孩把猫从河里救了出来。
senses.why: Italian bravo first described a bold, wild person, and that boldness became the heart of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 bravo 最初形容大胆、不驯的人，这种胆气后来成了这个词义的核心。

senses.title: To face danger or bad weather
senses.definition: to face danger, bad weather or difficulty in order to do something
senses.definitionCN: 为了做某事而直面危险、恶劣天气或困难
senses.example: The fishermen braved the storm to reach the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 渔民们冒着风暴驶向港口。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb: instead of running from the danger, a person goes out and meets it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了动词：人不是躲开危险，而是主动走出去迎上去。

senses.title: Fine and splendid
senses.definition: fine, splendid or showy, now mostly kept in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 美好的、壮丽的或引人注目的，今多保留在固定短语中
senses.example: They set out for a brave new world.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出发前往一个美丽的新世界。
senses.why: In older use brave meant showy and splendid, and this sense survives in a few set phrases.
senses.whyCN: 在较早的用法里 brave 意为华丽、壮美，这个义项只保留在少数固定短语中。

intro.en: Brave came through French and Italian from a word for wild and bold, and it has softened into praise.
intro.cn: brave 经由法语和意大利语来自一个意为「野性、大胆」的词，后来变成了赞美之词。

items.en: The trail starts at barbarus, a word for a foreigner seen as wild.
items.cn: 这条线索始于 barbarus，指被视为野性的外邦人。

items.en: Italian bravo meant bold, wild or ready to fight.
items.cn: 意大利语 bravo 意为大胆、不驯或随时准备动手。

items.en: French took the word and used it for a fine, showy and daring person.
items.cn: 法语借入这个词，用来形容出色、气派又胆大的人。

items.en: English borrowed it and made courage the main sense.
items.cn: 英语借入后，把「勇气」发展成了主要义项。

items.en: Today brave praises courage, and the verb means to face danger on purpose.
items.cn: 今天 brave 用来称赞勇气，动词则指有意直面危险。

note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与勇气有关的词。

definition_zh: 明天；明日；未来；将来
definition_en: the day after today, or the near future that has not come yet
core_image: 窗外的天色还没亮，桌上放着一张写着明日的车票
scene: 深夜的教室里，最后一盏灯也要熄了，值日生把黑板擦干净才走。 The exam is tomorrow morning, so everyone went to bed early.
sceneCN: 这里 tomorrow 是「明天」这一天（第 1 个义项：今天的下一天）；句意为考试就在明天上午，于是大家都早早上床。画面里有熄灯的教室、擦净的黑板与走廊。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加复数词尾 -s 构成，义为「一个又一个明天」
由同一构词模式 todæg 演化而来，义为「今天」
由同一构词模式构成的同族词，义为「今晚」

senses.title: The day after today
senses.definition: the day that follows the present day
senses.definitionCN: 紧接在今天之后的那一天
senses.example: We will finish the report tomorrow, before the office opens.
senses.exampleCN: 我们明天在办公室开门前把报告写完。
senses.why: The Old English form joins the word for morrow with the preposition to, so the word literally points at the next day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语形式把表示「次日」的词与介词 to 连在一起，字面上就是「指向下一天」。

senses.title: The near future
senses.definition: the time that is still to come, especially the near future
senses.definitionCN: 尚未到来的时间，尤指不久之后
senses.example: The engineers spoke of the city of tomorrow as if they could already walk in it.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师们谈起未来的城市，仿佛已经能在其中行走。
senses.why: One step beyond the next morning, the word becomes a name for any time not yet reached.
senses.whyCN: 再往前一步，这个词就成了任何尚未抵达之时间的名字。

senses.title: Morning as a time of day
senses.definition: in older usage, the morning hours of any day
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，任何一天的早晨时段
senses.example: Good morrow to you, the old greeting said, wishing a fine morning.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的问候语会说 good morrow，祝愿对方有个美好的早晨。
senses.why: The morrow of the word is the same morrow that meant morning, and that older sense survives in greetings.
senses.whyCN: 词中的 morrow 就是表示「早晨」的那个 morrow，这个古义在问候语里留了下来。

senses.title: A promise about the future
senses.definition: a pledge that something will be done on the next day or later
senses.definitionCN: 保证在某天或之后去做某事的承诺
senses.example: He kept saying tomorrow, and the fence was never painted.
senses.exampleCN: 他总说明天，篱笆却始终没有刷。
senses.why: Because the next day is always available in speech, tomorrow becomes the natural home of postponed promises.
senses.whyCN: 因为口语里永远还有下一个明天，tomorrow 就自然成了拖延承诺的落脚处。

senses.title: The next issue or edition
senses.definition: used in publishing for the edition that comes out on the next day
senses.definitionCN: 出版业中指第二天出的那一期
senses.example: The editor held the story for tomorrow's paper and let the evening edition go without it.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把这条新闻留到明天的报纸，晚报就先不带它。
senses.why: Editors work a day ahead, so the next day's date in a masthead is simply the word for the coming edition.
senses.whyCN: 编辑总是提前一天工作，于是报头上第二天的日期就顺理成章成了「下一期」的代称。

senses.title: A future opportunity
senses.definition: a chance that will appear later rather than now
senses.definitionCN: 以后而不是现在才出现的机会
senses.example: There is always tomorrow, said the coach, meaning the next match.
senses.exampleCN: 教练说总还有明天，意思是还有下一场比赛。
senses.why: When a loss must be comforted, the next day becomes the name of hope itself.
senses.whyCN: 需要安慰一场失利时，下一天就成了希望这个名字。

senses.title: The future as a shared project
senses.definition: the future considered as something a group works towards together
senses.definitionCN: 被视为一个群体共同为之努力的未来
senses.example: The village meeting was really about tomorrow, not about the drains.
senses.exampleCN: 村会的真正议题是未来，而不是下水道。
senses.why: The word can stand for the whole horizon a community plans for, once it stops meaning one date.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不再指某个日期，这个词就能代表一个共同体规划的整片地平线。

senses.title: Time treated as an ordinary commodity
senses.definition: the next day as a plain unit of scheduling, without emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 作为普通日程单位的下一天，不带强调
senses.example: Tomorrow suits me better than Friday, if that is all right.
senses.exampleCN: 如果方便的话，明天比周五更适合我。
senses.why: Here the word carries no weight beyond the calendar, which is how it appears in most everyday planning.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词除了日历之外不携带任何分量，多数日常安排里它就是这样出现的。

senses.title: The adverb of the next day
senses.definition: as an adverb, on the day following today
senses.definitionCN: 作副词时指在今天之后的那一天
senses.example: She will drive north tomorrow and be back by Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 她明天开车北上，周日之前回来。
senses.why: The noun and the adverb share one shape, so the word sits in a sentence without any preposition at all.
senses.whyCN: 名词与副词同形，因此这个词可以不带任何介词直接进入句子。

intro.en: Tomorrow is a native English compound: the preposition to joined to morrow, an old word for the next day or the morning.
intro.cn: tomorrow 是英语本土复合词：介词 to 加上 morrow（古义为次日、早晨）。

items.en: The word morgen means morning, and morrow in the phrase on the morrow refers to the following day.
items.cn: 古英语 morgen 意为早晨，短语 on the morrow 里的 morrow 指紧接着的那一天。

items.en: To morgen, written as two words, points forward to the next morning and is the direct ancestor of the modern form.
items.cn: 写作两个词的 to morgen 表示「到明天早晨」，是现代形式的直接祖先。

items.en: The two elements merge into a single word to morwe, later tomorrow, while morrow keeps the older sense separately.
items.cn: 两个成分合并为一词 to morwe，后来成为 tomorrow，而 morrow 另行保留古义。

items.en: The word settles into its present spelling in the sixteenth century and takes over the adverbial use from the phrase on the morrow.
items.cn: 这个词在十六世纪定下现在的拼写，并接替短语 on the morrow 的副词用法。

items.en: From the eighteenth century tomorrow extends beyond the next day to mean the indefinite future.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，tomorrow 由「次日」扩展到指不确定的未来。

items.en: In modern speech it also stands alone as a promise or a postponement, as in tomorrow and tomorrow and tomorrow.
items.cn: 现代口语里它也单独用作承诺或拖延的说法，正如「明天，明天，再一个明天」那一句。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other words of the same to- family in time words, while the near-meaning group gathers terms for the days and the future.
note.cn: 形近组收集时间词里由 to- 构成的同族词，近义组则汇集表示日期与未来的词。

normalIntro.en: These memories use the two parts of the compound, the fixed time phrases, and the family with today and tonight.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用复合词的两个部分、固定时间短语，以及和 today、tonight 构成的词族。

normal.en: To plus morrow: the word literally means towards the next morning.
normal.cn: to 加 morrow：这个词字面意为「向着下一个早晨」。

normal.en: Tomorrow morning and tomorrow afternoon keep the noun before the time of day.
normal.cn: tomorrow morning 与 tomorrow afternoon 把名词放在具体时段之前。

normal.en: Today, tonight, and tomorrow all begin with to-, a small family for pointing at time.
normal.cn: today、tonight、tomorrow 都以 to- 开头，是专门指向时间的小词族。

normal.en: Morrow is the second half, and it survives alone in literary English.
normal.cn: morrow 是后半部分，在书面语里仍单独使用。

normal.en: There is no preposition: we say I will go tomorrow, not on tomorrow.
normal.cn: 这里不用介词：说 I will go tomorrow，而不是 on tomorrow。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at a door that is still closed, and the closed door is tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手正指向一扇还没打开的门，那扇门就是明天。

abstract.en: Think of a note left on the table that says only: tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想桌上留了一张纸条，上面只写着：明天。

abstract.en: Every evening the word is handed back to you, empty again, ready to be filled.
abstract.cn: 每天傍晚这个词又被交还给你，空白如初，等着被填满。

examples.en: I will call you tomorrow after lunch.
examples.cn: 我明天午饭后给你打电话。

examples.en: Tomorrow's train leaves at six in the morning.
examples.cn: 明天的火车早上六点开。

examples.en: The planners kept talking about the city of tomorrow.
examples.cn: 规划者一直在谈未来的城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特玛柔」——拉着特玛柔的手说，明天再来，就是明天。

root: 古英语 to morgen（到明天早晨）→ 中古英语 to morwe → tomorrow。由介词 to 与 morrow（次日、早晨；古英语 morgen）合成；同族词有 today、tonight。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the plain date that follows today, then widens to the near future, the old sense of morning, promises, editions, and finally the adverb that needs no preposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从紧接今天的那个日期写起，再扩到不久的将来、早晨的古义、承诺、报刊的一期，最后是不带介词的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointing towards the next morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指指向下一个早晨。

branches.en: The next day as a date and as an ordinary schedule unit.
branches.cn: 作为日期与普通日程单位的下一天。

branches.en: The future as time, as opportunity, and as a shared project.
branches.cn: 作为时间、机会与共同事业的未来。

branches.en: The old sense of morning kept in greetings.
branches.cn: 在问候语里保留的早晨古义。

branches.en: The next day used to postpone.
branches.cn: 用来拖延的下一天。

branches.en: The next day in publishing and editions.
branches.cn: 出版领域里的次日一期。

intro.en: The word is a native compound of a preposition and a noun, and its endings are only the plural -s and its fixed time phrases.

items.example: The ending appears in both morrow and tomorrow.

senses.title: Vessel
senses.definition: a large boat for carrying people or goods at sea
senses.definitionCN: 在海上运送人或货物的大型船
senses.example: The ship sailed into the harbour.

senses.why: This is the basic nautical sense.

senses.title: To transport
senses.definition: to send goods by ship or another carrier

senses.example: The company ships orders every morning.

senses.why: The vessel becomes the act of sending.
senses.whyCN: 船引申为运送的动作。

senses.title: To release
senses.definition: to make a product available to customers
senses.definitionCN: 把产品交付给客户
senses.example: The studio will ship the game next month.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室下个月将发布这款游戏。
senses.why: Software borrowed the transport image.
senses.whyCN: 软件业借用了运输的意象。

senses.title: To send away
senses.definition: to send someone somewhere, often quickly

senses.why: Sending cargo extends to sending people.

items.en: Scip meant a seagoing vessel.

items.en: Skip shared the same seafaring root.

items.en: Ship covered both the vessel and the voyage.

items.en: Ship became a verb meaning to send goods.

note.en: Ship is compared with similar-looking words and with words for boats.

abstract.en: Cargo and news travel on the same hull.

abstract.en: To ship is to trust your work to the sea.

examples.en: The company ships orders every morning.
